name: Peach-bloom glaze (a copper red, reduction-fired, mottled pink, red and green, over porcelain)

diffuseAlbedo.source: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, 14.40.377, photograph DP246426.jpg (CC0); MuseeVision/Scripts/vessels.py glaze_colour
diffuseAlbedo.derivation: The median of the glaze where the fitted camera sees the vase within 30 degrees of face on, its highlights (the brightest tenth) left out, relative to the photograph's own white (its 99.5th percentile of lightness, the white lip where the glaze runs thin, taken as L* 100).

refractiveIndex.source: Substances/low-iron-glass.json (1.523 for soda-lime float); a ceramic glaze is a soda-lime-alumina-silica glass of about the same index

porosity.derivation: a fired glaze has no open pores

wettingDepth.derivation: with no pores, nothing wets its body

grain.note: The bubbles held in the glaze.

bed.note: The mottle's patches, read by eye: a few millimetres to two centimetres across.

hurst.source: Candela et al. 2012, Journal of Geophysical Research 117, B08409 (fault surfaces, 0.6 to 0.8; cited in Stone.ush)
hurst.note: The middle of the range measured on rock surfaces, as the travertine's.

toneSpread.derivation: The standard deviation of ln(lightness) over the glaze seen within 37 degrees of face on, its shading taken out (less its blur over 20 cells, 1.6 cm), highlights left out: the mottle.

roughnessSpread.note: A first half-range of ln(roughness) across one face.
